description: Use when the user asks to rebuild, clone, copy, port, restyle or 'make it look like' part of a real website, or wants a site's section as Tailwind, HTML+CSS, React (JSX) or Vue. Give it the URL and, when the user named a part of the page, section (hero, header, footer, pricing, features, testimonials, faq, cta) - never invent a CSS selector. With neither, it auto-detects the hero; every call also returns `sections`, each other extractable section with a label and a ready selector for a follow-up call. Returns a self-contained component with the page's real resolved styles (true colors, fonts, spacing, copy) plus the tokens and assets it uses, so you adapt real values instead of estimating from a screenshot. For jsx/vue, repeated structures collapse into a data array rendered with .map()/v-for; ::before/::after come back as real elements; @keyframes ship in the css field. The `theme` field says which theme the code actually is - sites with a prefers-color-scheme dark variant return the light branch unless you pass theme='dark'; say which you returned. Not for: whole-page scraping, page text, or sites that need a login. Reads static HTML/CSS by default; if the result is thin or carries a `hint`, call again with render=true (+5 credits).

fresh.description: Skip the 24-hour cache and re-extract the live page - use when the site just changed and a cached result would be stale. Charged normally; the fresh result replaces the cached copy.

name.description: Component name for the jsx target (default ExtractedSection). Ignored by tailwind, html and vue. Renaming never re-runs the extraction - it costs 0 credits on a cached section.

render.description: Run the page in a real browser first so its JavaScript executes - use for client-rendered (React/Next/SPA) sites, when a normal call came back thin, or after a 403 target_blocked (bot protection refuses plain HTTP requests but usually lets a browser through). Slower, and adds 5 credits to the call. Paid API plans and credit packs only: on a free account it returns 402 render_requires_plan and nothing runs - never pass it as a first attempt, and when a free account gets that error, retry without it and tell the user this page needs JS rendering, a paid feature. Free accounts still get rendering automatically when the SITE refuses the plain request (401/403/406): the server retries it in a browser at no charge, a few times a month, and the result carries usage.renderRescue explaining what happened - read that sentence out to the user when it appears.

screenshot.description: Requires render=true. Adds a screenshot field to the result: a public URL of a capture of the page (live 7 days), taken by the same browser that rendered it. Pass true for the 1440x900 viewport or 'full' for the entire page height. No extra credits beyond the render surcharge. Useful for showing the user what the extracted site looks like.

section.description: Which part of the page, by name - use this when the user asked for the pricing, footer, header/nav, features, testimonials, FAQ or call-to-action block. Resolved on the page itself from its ids, classes, headings and, failing those, its content (prices, blockquotes, FAQ items), so it works without seeing the markup and on pages that label nothing. Omit for the hero. If the page has no such section you get the hero plus a `note` listing what is there.

selector.description: CSS selector for the section, ONLY when you have one from a previous result's `sections` list (e.g. "section.pricing-grid"). Do not guess selectors: a selector that matches nothing falls back to the hero with a `note`, and the guess costs a call. Prefer `section` for named parts of a page.

theme.description: Which colour scheme to extract (default light). Pass 'dark' when the user is looking at the site in dark mode or asks for the dark version: the page's prefers-color-scheme: dark rules and custom properties become the component itself instead of riding along as dark: variants. Works whether the site expresses its themes as @media (prefers-color-scheme) or as a root attribute/class the CSS is scoped to ([data-theme=dark], html.dark). Sites that switch themes purely in JavaScript cannot be selected this way - you get the page default plus a hint saying so. No extra credits.

name: extract_code

autoDetected.description: True when the hero was auto-detected rather than passed in

code.description: The generated, paste-ready component code. For jsx/vue, repeated structures (tiers, cards, list items) are collapsed into a data array rendered with .map()/v-for

css.description: Companion CSS: always set for framework=html; for other frameworks it carries the @keyframes the section uses (add to the global stylesheet)

hint.description: Only present when the extraction looks degraded (client-rendered page, runtime-injected styles) - says what to do: on a static call usually retry with render=true; on a render=true call the styles could not be resolved even in a browser, do not retry

note.description: Present when the requested selector or section was not found and the hero was returned instead - says what was asked for and which sections the page does have. Tell the user.

section.description: The named section that was resolved, when one was requested

sections.description: Every extractable section on the page - call again with one of these selectors for a specific part

selector.description: The CSS selector that was extracted

summary.description: What was extracted, at a glance. styledCoverage (0-100) is the quality signal: the % of elements the cascade found styles for

theme.description: light | dark: which one the code you just received actually is. Measured from the page, never echoed from your request - so if you asked for a theme the site cannot serve, this reports what you really got. Tell the user which theme they got when it may not match what they see on the site

tokens.description: Design tokens the extracted section actually uses

truncation_note.description: Present when the result was trimmed - says what was dropped and how to get more.

usage.description: Credit usage for the authed key (spent, remaining, monthly limit).

title: Extract section as code
